niche: the credit loss an Irish commercial property lender should plan for 2027 when its security values are quarterly index roll-forwards of inspections mostly made before 2020 and its loss given default haircut was fitted on valuations made at default
analyst_test: A strong analyst takes each loan's 2027 default chance from the master scale and its exposure at 31 December 2026, prices the loss with the bank's loss given default model (its sale haircut on the security value the property register carries, the last inspection rolled forward by the commercial property index), back-tests the model on the 2012 to 2026 defaults at their valuations at default, where it passes, and files a 2027 credit loss well under the golden.
domain_test: The 2027 expected credit loss of a commercial property book is default chance times exposure times loss given default, and the loss turns on what the security fetches if the borrower fails; the decisive step reads credit's own collateral mechanics (an inspection at default, an index roll-forward, a sale haircut, and the selection of which borrowers fail), and with another field's nouns there is no security value whose drift is selected by the very failure being priced.

spine.entity: one commercial property loan facility at one month end

world.geography: Ireland (a fictional commercial property lender headquartered in Galway, lending across the Republic)
world.org_type: a licensed bank lending to small and medium businesses on commercial property

driver: The decisive quantity is what a unit's security fetches if the unit fails, which the record measures by an inspection made at the failure while the forward units carry only a market index rolled forward from an earlier inspection; the security of units that fail falls behind the index by more the longer since that inspection, and the forward units were inspected longer ago than the record's failures mostly were, so the rolled-forward index overstates what the failing units will fetch.
driver_concrete: Each commercial property loan's 2027 loss turns on what its property sells for if the borrower defaults: Ardcarn's loss given default haircut was fitted on valuations made at default, the 2026 book carries quarterly index roll-forwards of inspections mostly made before 2020, and in the bank's own record a defaulter's property was valued at default below its rolled-forward index value by more the older its last inspection.
stump: A competent solver applies the bank's haircut to the security values the property register carries at 31 December 2026, weights each loan by its master-scale default chance and exposure, sees the model back-test cleanly on the 2012 to 2026 defaults at their valuations at default, and files a 2027 credit loss well under the golden; the step that lands it there is taking the rolled-forward index value as the value the bank will sell at.
deep_chain: (1) the 2027 loss is each loan's default chance times exposure times loss given default, with the bank's haircut model at rung 0; (2) the haircut was fitted on inspections made at default while the book carries index roll-forwards of older inspections, so the model's input differs between its fit and its use; (3) in the record a defaulter's inspection at default sits below its rolled-forward index value by an amount that grows with the years since its last inspection; (4) the 2026 book was last inspected longer ago than most of the record's defaulters; (5) each loan's expected value at default is its rolled-forward value cut by its own staleness shortfall, run through the haircut and the floor to the 2027 loss.
judgment: The shortfall of value at default against the rolled-forward index as a function of years since the last inspection, a selection effect (borrowers fail when their property has fallen behind the market) estimated by regression on the record's defaults that carry both values, and applied to each loan's own staleness, inside the range the record covers.
one_fact_test: The likeliest hint, that valuations at default come in below the indexed value, still leaves the solver to find that the shortfall grows with staleness (an average shortfall files the record's mix, not the book's), to read each loan's staleness by walking its valuation history past the quarterly roll-forward rows, and to carry it through the haircut's floor loan by loan.
strategy_label: WORKS IN FORM: heterogeneity that pooling hides, the shortfall differing by staleness and the decision weighting it to a book staler than the record, the staleness rebuilt from the valuation history and never read off a column.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many of the period's placeable units a fixed team can finish before the period closes, because each unit counts only once that team performs one last step for it, the team's spare weekly capacity is visible only as the ceiling it held through an earlier unrelated surge, and the decision's own volume, bunched by its filed calendar into weeks no closed period approached, queues the later units past the close; the closed record's lag and an annual capacity check both pass, so the placeable count overstates the in-period total wherever the team is small and the units are many.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a forward total projected from a history of cumulative progress by age in which the units carrying most of the amount began resolving more slowly partway through the record; the share of the amount settled tracks the share of units resolved rather than age, so the history has to be restated at the resolution shares the latest observations show before its age-to-age ratios are carried forward, and carrying them unrestated, or taking them from the latest periods alone, understates the total.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the part of each unit's recorded wait that the offered intervention removes, because the recorded wait fuses the step the intervention replaces with a concurrent step it leaves in place, so only the replaced step's excess over the concurrent one, built by joining separate operational logs, counts; ranking units by the recorded wait, or by the replaced step measured from the same start, credits the units whose concurrent step is slowest.
